channel.title: Dads for Christ
channel.description: Encouragement for fathers, families, faith, leadership, and living boldly for Jesus Christ.

item.title: Dwell With Her
item.description: First Peter 3:7 calls a husband to dwell with his wife according to knowledge, to give her honor, and to see her as a fellow heir of the grace of life, so that his prayers are not hindered. When a man is present and understanding, his wife is steadied, the children who watch learn what a husband is, and the home takes a gentler tone than distance leaves behind.

item.title: Redeeming the Time
item.description: Ephesians 5:15–16 calls a man to walk circumspectly and redeem the time, because the days are evil, and Psalm 90:12 asks God to teach him to number his days. The hours with his wife and children are a stewardship to spend now, with the phone down, at the table, in bedtime prayer, and listening, instead of handing the house only what a busy day leaves over.

item.title: Fight for Your House
item.description: Nehemiah 4:14 calls a man not to be afraid, but to remember the Lord and fight for his brethren, his sons, his daughters, his wife, and his house. He stands that post by being present and praying beside his wife, one hand on the work and the other on the watch, instead of withdrawing when pressure, discouragement, and spiritual attack come.

item.title: Provoke Not Your Children
item.description: Ephesians 6:4 and Colossians 3:21 call a man not to provoke his children to anger, but to bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. When he is present and patient, the children are not discouraged, his wife is not left alone in the home, and the house learns gentleness instead of wrath.

item.title: Call Her Blessed
item.description: Proverbs 31:28 calls a husband to praise his wife where she can hear it, and Numbers 6:24–26 is a blessing a present man can pray over his children. When his mouth gives life, his wife is honored, his children are named with hope, and the home takes a gentler tone.

item.title: Iron Sharpens Iron
item.description: A man was never meant to fight for his marriage, his children, and his faith alone. Proverbs 27:17 calls him to walk with godly men who sharpen, confess, and pray, so he comes home more present and steadier, and goes after the one man who has drifted.

item.title: Stand Fast
item.description: First Corinthians 16:13–14 calls a man to be watchful, steady in the faith, courageous, and strong, and to do all of it in love. When his strength is gentle and his love is steady, his wife, his children, and his home are held.

item.title: Turn the Hearts
item.description: Malachi 4:6 and Luke 1:17 call for a father's heart to turn toward his children. When that turning is real, a child is known, a wife is no longer alone in the raising, and a home is made ready for the Lord.

item.title: Two Are Better Than One
item.description: A husband and wife face stress, money, illness, conflict, and spiritual attack together. Ecclesiastes 4:9–12 calls a man to stand with his wife, with Christ as the third strand, so his wife, his children, and his home are held.

item.title: Go After the One
item.description: Jesus leaves the ninety and nine to go after the one lost sheep. The first mission field for a man is his own home, then the one man who has wandered from God, and being present is how he goes after them.

item.title: As for Me and My House
item.description: Joshua 24:15 calls a man to decide, and to lead, that his household will serve the Lord. When he is present in worship, his wife, his children, and his home receive a clear direction in a busy age.

item.title: Do Not Grow Weary
item.description: The long work of a husband and a present father can make a man want to quit. Galatians 6:9 calls him to keep doing good at home, and a wife, a child, and a house are steadied when he does not give up.

item.title: Love Her as Christ
item.description: A man who loves his wife as Christ loved the church spends himself for her good, and that love steadies the marriage, teaches the children, and gives the home the shape of Jesus.

item.title: A Soft Answer
item.description: Anger rises in every marriage and every home. A man who answers softly turns the heat down, protects his wife and children, and shows them Christ.

item.title: Before the Sun Goes Down
item.description: Husbands and wives face anger together. A man who will not let the sun go down on his wrath keeps bitterness from settling on his wife, his children, and his home.

item.title: Teach Them Diligently
item.description: Faith is handed down at the dinner table, in the truck, and at bedtime, when a man talks of God's words there and not only on Sunday.

item.title: A Place of Refuge
item.description: A present father gives his children a refuge, stands beside his wife, and teaches the home whom it serves.

item.title: Pray With Her
item.description: Husbands and wives face real battles together. A husband who takes the lead in praying with his wife strengthens the marriage and the home.

item.title: More Than a Paycheck
item.description: A paycheck can keep a household, and God calls a father to provide. Children still need his time, his attention, and a man who will lead them to Jesus.

item.title: Stay in the Room
item.description: Husbands and wives fight real battles. A father who stays in the room — listening, repenting, and praying — changes the temperature of the home.

item.title: What It Means to Reach One
item.description: Jesus left the ninety-nine to go after the one. That same mission still matters today. Who is the one person God may be calling you to pray for, encourage, and point back to Him?
